examples.title: Plate With Mounting Holes
examples.lesson: Holes are cut by extruding the hole profile and boolean-subtracting it from the body.

examples.title: Cylinder With Bore
examples.lesson: Concentric circles in one sketch extrude directly into a tube, no boolean needed.

examples.title: Open Top Box
examples.lesson: Shell a solid with a negative thickness and the end cap face to open the top.

examples.title: Cup With Handle
examples.lesson: Shell the cup from its top cap, build the handle as a ring on a perpendicular plane, union it on.

examples.title: Revolved Vase
examples.lesson: Closed profile = axis line + spline + closing lines; the revolve axis is a Line value, never a query.

examples.title: Square To Round Transition
examples.lesson: Each loft profile is its own solved sketch on its own plane; opLoft takes profileSubqueries.

examples.title: Swept Curved Tube
examples.lesson: Sweep needs an open path wire and a profile sketch on a plane perpendicular to the path start.

examples.title: L Bracket With Fillet
examples.lesson: Closed polyline profile + one extrude; fillet edges via qEdgeTopologyFilter over the body edges.

examples.title: Bolt Circle Flange
examples.lesson: Loop with var + trig places bolt holes in the SAME sketch; string ids use the ~ operator.

examples.title: Base With Corner Posts
examples.lesson: Build each component as its own extrude, position via offset planes, union into one body.

examples.title: Stepped Shaft With Chamfer
examples.lesson: Stack sections on offset planes, union them, then chamfer the body edges.

examples.title: Disc With Circular Patterned Bosses
examples.lesson: Circular patterns use opPattern with rotationAround transforms and instanceNames (opPatternCircular does NOT exist); the original body is preserved so loop from 1.

examples.title: Heatsink With Linear Patterned Fins
examples.lesson: Linear patterns use opPattern with transform(direction * spacing * i) translations and instanceNames (opPatternLinear does NOT exist).

examples.title: Pen With Tip And Clip
examples.lesson: Everyday objects decompose into recognizable components — a pen is a barrel cylinder + lofted tapered tip + pocket clip, never one stretched primitive.

examples.title: Bottle With Neck
examples.lesson: A bottle is a revolved profile with belly, shoulder, and narrower neck, then shelled hollow through the neck opening; never a plain cylinder.

examples.title: Hex Bolt
examples.lesson: A bolt = hex polygon head + cylindrical shaft on an offset plane + union + tip chamfer.

examples.title: Hex Nut
examples.lesson: A nut is a hex polygon with a concentric bore circle in the SAME sketch, extruded once — never a bolt shaft with no head, and never a bolt-with-shaft template reused for a nut.

examples.title: Wheel With Spokes
examples.lesson: A wheel = rim ring + hub ring with axle bore + one spoke circular-patterned via opPattern, all unioned.

examples.title: Picture Frame
examples.lesson: A frame is a rectangular ring: outer and inner rectangles in the SAME sketch extrude into the border with the middle open.

examples.title: Sphere
examples.lesson: A sphere is a semicircle arc plus a closing line drawn exactly on the axis, revolved 360 degrees; the closing line must be coincident with the revolve axis.

examples.title: Torus
examples.lesson: A torus is a circle offset from (never touching) the revolve axis, revolved 360 degrees.

examples.title: D-Shaft
examples.lesson: A D-shaft is a round shaft with an oversized rectangular tool boolean-subtracted past one side to leave a single flat face.

examples.title: Knurled Knob
examples.lesson: Knurling is a thin radial groove tool circular-patterned with opPattern around the knob axis, then boolean-subtracted from the base cylinder (not unioned, since it removes material).

examples.title: Wedge Ramp
examples.lesson: A ramp/wedge is a closed right-triangle profile (base, vertical back, sloped hypotenuse) extruded once.
